root_idea.title: Syllable-Aligned Reference Prosody Conditioning for F5-TTS Chinese

components.name: Syllable-aligned reference prosody summary
components.description: Extract fixed-dimensional pitch, energy, normalized duration, and coarse temporal trend statistics from the reference audio, aggregate them over the existing pinyin syllable sequence, and inject the resulting embeddings through the existing text-conditioning path. The representation is trained jointly with the full F5-TTS model, so requires_training is true.

components.name: Prosody-preserving batch transform
components.description: During training, preserve the existing text and mel targets while deriving reference summaries from the conditioning audio. Normalize speaker-level statistics before injection so the representation carries relative timing and intonation rather than absolute speaker identity.

components.name: Existing flow-matching and inference contract
components.description: Keep the DiT architecture, conditional flow-matching objective, pinyin vocabulary, Vocos mel interface, vocoder, 32-step inference default, CFG conditioning, eight-NPU BF16 training, FP32 master parameters, 50 epochs, and final EMA selection unchanged unless the candidate action requires the corresponding workspace source edit.

root_idea.abstract: F5-TTS Chinese generation currently relies on a flat pinyin-conditioned flow model and implicit prosody inference. This refinement adds a compact reference-derived prosody summary aligned to the existing pinyin syllable sequence, combining normalized pitch, energy, duration, and coarse temporal trend information. The summary is injected through the existing conditioning path and trained with the complete Premium split using official initialization, a fresh optimizer, eight NPUs, BF16 autocast, FP32 master parameters, 50 epochs, and final EMA weights. The fixed tokenizer, mel representation, vocoder, and Paraformer CER evaluation remain unchanged.
root_idea.core_contribution: The contribution is a local repair to the baseline's flat prosody assumption: syllable-aligned reference statistics provide an explicit bridge between Chinese linguistic units and acoustic timing while retaining the existing conditional flow-matching model. The mechanism should reduce prosodic averaging and long-context timing drift without changing the content representation or vocoder.
root_idea.method: Prepare an isolated workspace source and implement the intervention in the existing F5-TTS conditioning or batch transformation slots. For each training and inference example, compute speaker-normalized reference pitch and energy trajectories, coarse duration or pace descriptors, and temporal trend summaries; align them to the existing pinyin syllable sequence using the reference text's syllable boundaries, then interpolate or repeat them to the mel conditioning length. Concatenate or add the resulting embeddings to the existing text conditioning representation and train all resulting parameters from official pretrained weights with the fixed 50-epoch Premium protocol. Use the normal SURE candidate execution with requires_training=true, final EMA weights, and the unchanged Paraformer CER route.
root_idea.risks: Reference text and audio may have imperfect syllable boundaries, causing alignment noise. Pitch extraction can fail on unvoiced or noisy regions, and normalization may remove useful speaker cues. Additional conditioning may over-transfer reference prosody, reduce content robustness, increase memory use, or provide little CER benefit if the baseline already infers timing adequately.
target_defects: Flat implicit prosody representation in the baseline
Weak synchronization between Chinese syllable structure and acoustic timing
Entanglement of reference speaker style with local pronunciation and duration
root_idea.rationale: This is the smallest mechanism-level patch supported by the survey. The survey explicitly identifies hierarchical linguistic timing as a missing capability and identifies accurate synchronization as the central implementation constraint. A syllable-level reference summary stays inside the existing conditioning and training slots, preserves the current F5-TTS thesis, and targets Chinese intelligibility through timing and pronunciation stability rather than through a numeric sweep or a new control architecture.
